definitions.explanation: A preliminary version of a document, plan, or law that is subject to revision. Commonly used in legal, political, and business contexts. Composed of 草 (grass/rough) + 案 (plan/idea).

examples.japanese: {法案|ほうあん}の{草案|そうあん}が{提出|ていしゅつ}された。
examples.english: A draft of the bill was submitted.

examples.japanese: {委員会|いいんかい}で{草案|そうあん}を{検討|けんとう}する。
examples.english: The committee will review the draft.

examples.japanese: {憲法|けんぽう}{改正|かいせい}の{草案|そうあん}をめぐって{激|はげ}しい{議論|ぎろん}が{交|か}わされた。
examples.english: Heated debate was exchanged over the draft constitutional amendment.

notes:
USAGE:
{草案|そうあん} is a formal word most commonly used in political, legal, and bureaucratic contexts. It implies a document that is still subject to review and revision before being finalized.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {草案|そうあん}を{作成|さくせい}する (prepare a draft)
- {草案|そうあん}を{提出|ていしゅつ}する (submit a draft)
- {草案|そうあん}を{検討|けんとう}する (review a draft)
- {草案|そうあん}をまとめる (put together a draft)
- {憲法|けんぽう}{草案|そうあん} (constitutional draft)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{下書|したが}き means "rough draft" and is used more generally for any written draft. {原案|げんあん} means "original plan" or "original draft" and suggests the first version of a proposal. {素案|そあん} is a very preliminary draft or outline.
